issues.description: Crash-log path complects buffering lifecycle with recording configuration and OTLP handler discovery.
issues.detail: Three concerns are intertwined: (1) whether to buffer, (2) whether/when to initialize recording, (3) finding the OTLP handler by isinstance scan. _on_cleanup synthesizes a RecordingOptions with logs=True regardless of what the user/server asked. Separate the buffer (a value: list of records) from the sink decision (a policy) from handler discovery (keep a direct reference at install time).

issues.description: Handler discovery by isinstance scan over root logger handlers is place-oriented and fragile.
issues.detail: Both _flush_early_log_buffer and _shutdown_telemetry iterate root.handlers looking for a LoggingHandler instance. That couples this module to global mutable state and to whoever else may have added or wrapped that handler. Hold the handler returned by _setup_cloud_tracer as a value/identity on the JobContext and address it directly.

issues.description: Unbounded in-memory log buffer with no cap, no drop policy, no time bound.
issues.detail: _BufferingHandler.buffer grows without limit between _start_log_buffering and either flush or cleanup. A job that crashes slowly, or a chatty library at DEBUG, can balloon memory before the worker ever notices. Make the buffer a bounded ring (size or bytes), and decide explicitly what to drop. The buffer is a value; give it a defined shape.

issues.description: Shutdown handler removal mutates global logging state and can silently drop later log routing.
issues.detail: _shutdown_telemetry now strips every LoggingHandler from the root logger before force_flush. Any non-OTLP LoggingHandler the user installed is collateral. The essential problem (re-entrant emit during flush) deserves a narrower fix: remove only the handler this module installed, by reference, not by type scan.

issues.description: Unrelated worker.py reorder and makefile/test changes complect this PR's intent.
issues.detail: Reordering _pending_assignments registration before queuing availability_resp, disabling pytest -n auto, dropping test_plugin_google_stt, and the test_ipc retry-batch change are all separate facts about the world. They may each be correct, but bundling them with the crash-log feature makes the value of this change harder to reason about and to revert.

issues.description: _on_entry_done forces shutdown_fut on any exception, conflating crash with normal task exception semantics.
issues.detail: Setting _shutdown_fut with reason='job crashed' from a done-callback complects task failure with shutdown identity. If shutdown_fut is later awaited expecting a user-initiated value, the meaning of that value just got broader. Make the reason a typed value (CRASH vs USER vs TIMEOUT) and ensure consumers branch on it; don't overload one future with two life events.

review.summary: The intent is right — crash logs are facts the operator needs, and burying them inside session.start() complects "the job ran" with "we can see what happened." But the implementation entangles three separable concerns: a buffer (value), a sink policy (when/whether to upload), and OTLP handler discovery (identity). Today those are smeared across JobContext, _on_cleanup, _flush_early_log_buffer, and _shutdown_telemetry, with isinstance scans over global logger state holding it together. Decompose: hold the OTLP handler by reference, give the buffer a bounded shape, and let _on_cleanup ask a policy "should we upload crash logs?" rather than synthesize RecordingOptions inline. Also: the worker.py reorder, makefile change, and test_ipc edits are separate stories and should travel separately.
